item: row 332 (R797): whole-file rewrite is sparse-aware and disk-safe in both erasers; failed overwrites make the result not clean
summary: A whole rewrite writes only the data regions (SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE, else the logical size) and checks free space before every chunk, stopping before 64 MiB would be left; a stop is 'partially overwritten' (bytes done of bytes known), never destroyed, the file still deleted, the result 'may be incomplete'. Salt pages, key files and the logs that hold salt copies are never held to the reserve. Revision 3: a file it could not overwrite at all (not partial, not unreachable) is counted as not_overwritten and makes the result not clean. Two strings x12 (Plan-approved 2026-11-22), CLI lines, watcher log lines.
